      The story

      I’m Chrispreme, aka the Black Tiger. I’ve been skateboarding since 2016–2017, when I was 11 years old. Right now I’m about to turn 21, so you do the math.

      Through skating, I’ve learned a lot of lessons. I broke my ankle. I had to quit skating. I had to come back. I’ve had to try, and try again, time after time.

      Some days felt like I couldn’t skate at all, like I was the worst skater out there. Other days felt like I was on top, like everything was aligning. But through it all, I pushed through. And we’re still here today: still skating, still doing it.

      Skateboarding is way more than a sport. It’s a lifestyle, and it’s not an easy one.

      Being able to keep up this lifestyle and keep doing it is part of what makes skateboarding so special.

      Video editing.

      Skateboarding footage and short-form edits.

      How I got into editing

      Throughout my years of skating, a lot of things have lined up with skateboarding. One of those things was video editing.

      When I’m skating, I’m constantly checking the clips and making adjustments.

      When I check the clips, I can see what I’m doing right and what I’m doing wrong.

      That’s what really led me to start editing. After I made a video, I wanted it to look a certain way.

      That drove me to teach myself how to edit: color grading, sound, all the different parts of it. Now I’m at the point where I can pretty much edit things the way I want them, and that’s a great skill to have.
